# Einleitung

This handout demonstrates the PHBern page header, hierarchy, callouts, tables,
citations, cross-format website links, and the protected-resource marker.

::: {.callout-tip title="Zeitbudget"}
Plan approximately 30 minutes for this compact example.
:::

# Auftrag

## Analyse

Read the short [free example resource](../resources_free/example-resource.md)
and compare it with the
[protected example resource](../resources_non_free/example-reading.md).

The rendered PDF turns both relative paths into links under the
`website.site-url` configured in `_quarto.yml`. The protected link also
receives a lock marker.

## Fragen

1. Which information belongs in a course website?
2. Which information should remain in a protected institutional system?
3. How would you explain the difference to students?

::: {.callout-important title="Grundsatz"}
A visual lock marker communicates restricted intent; access control must be
implemented by the publishing platform.
:::

```{=typst}
#pagebreak()
```

# Evidence-informed design

Use citations in the ordinary Quarto form. For example, multimedia design
should manage cognitive processing rather than simply add media
[@mayer2021].

| Decision | Question |
|---|---|
| Text | Is every sentence needed for the task? |
| Image | Does it explain, orient, or motivate? |
| Interaction | What should learners think or produce? |
| Link | Will the target remain reachable after export? |

::: {.callout-note title="Source and automatic elements"}
The [source of this PDF example](https://github.com/PHBern-RConrardy/phbern-is1/blob/main/examples/handout.qmd)
shows the Markdown used for each element. The PHBern header, font, table of
contents, and bibliography heading are supplied by `phbern-typst`.
:::
